leads.summary: Deleting every BOOTX64.EFI hook leaves alternate UEFI deployment paths without a matching signed upgrade
leads.consequence: For an existing ISO installation using bootloader_config.removable=true, the installer writes the same hook to deploy /EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI. This migration deletes it and only re-signs /boot/EFI/limine/limine_x64.efi. The packaged 80-limine-efi-deploy.hook invokes limine-install, whose fallback update writes BOOTX64.EFI when ENABLE_LIMINE_FALLBACK=yes (Omarchy stock), but the post-hook only signs the primary limine_x64.efi. Unless another mechanism separately registered/signs the fallback, firmware booting the removable path encounters an unsigned loader under Secure Boot after a Limine upgrade. A pre-mounted install with custom boot.esp_path/efi_binary also loses its only updater: native limine-install deploys only the primary and optional fallback, never the custom destination, so its registered firmware target stays stale. Limit migration deletion to the primary UEFI variant or explicitly handle/sign each actual target path, and test all ISO variants.
leads.triage: Opus follow-up 1; No configurator layout regresses; only custom autoinstall esp_path/efi_binary with failed NVRAM registration loses updates (never signed). Not published; limine-install coverage statement published as verified context.; behavioural

leads.summary: Existing single or permissive VFAT masks are mistaken for restricted /boot
leads.consequence: An fstab option set containing dmask=0022 but no fmask (or fmask=0022 but no dmask) satisfies the outer `(fmask|dmask)` guard, so the migration never adds the missing mask. Even a pair of non-0077 masks is accepted. The earlier chmod calls cannot durably change FAT mount permissions; the boot directory or its files remain accessible to other users across remount/reboot. Check both effective masks and values separately rather than treating any mention of either as sufficient. This is separate from the previously reported genfstab-padding mismatch.
leads.triage: coordinator read lines 12,16; Opus rv3 synthetic fstab runs; Confirmed with single-space qualifier; published in F4 row; factual

leads.summary: Open #13462 independently rewrites the same ESP preflight and tests, a direct head-to-head conflict
leads.consequence: #13462 is not stacked (GitHub compare returned diverged; it is MERGEABLE against its own base). Both replace the same old root free-space check and append incompatible ESP algorithms: this PR checks a fixed 300 MiB, #13462 checks 2x the largest existing EFI image and skips when ESP shares root. Applying git merge-file using #13462's actual base produces conflict markers in both files; the current PR's tests cannot run on an unresolved merge. Choose one behavior and unify the fixtures before either merges after the other. Both target the same free-space gate before omarchy-update snapshots; this is not just a textual overlap.
leads.triage: coordinator merge-file of both heads (scratch), Opus merge13462.log; Confirmed; published as Related open PR note; factual

leads.summary: New migration test passes when the root-only ESP fix is removed
leads.consequence: The EFI fixture is a regular file inside a test-owned directory, and sudo is an exec-only stub. The previous bug, probing the EFI as the unprivileged caller rather than through as_root, is not caught: replacing `as_root test -f "$efi"` with `test -f "$efi" in a copy of the current migration still produces a passing test (including the re-run). On an actual root-only ESP the replaced predicate would be false, sbctl would never run and the UEFI loader would remain unsigned. Add an assertion on a stubbed privileged `test -f` invocation or use a controlled fixture that makes the unprivileged existence probe fail but the elevated probe succeed.
leads.triage: coordinator inspected Sol mutant run; Opus rv3 reproduced; Published as Optional test improvement; corroboration of Opus test gap

leads.summary: Open #10396 adds an existing-install SDDM migration but deliberately keeps the session line this PR removes only for new installs
leads.consequence: If #10396 also merges, its migration strips -auth/-password from existing sddm-autologin but leaves -session pam_gnome_keyring.so auto_start. This PR's install/login/sddm.sh and upgrade-to-quattro cover only new installs and 3-to-4 upgrades. Existing 4.x installs retain the session entry even after both migrations. The two install scripts merge without conflict but duplicate auth/password sed lines; #10396's own test explicitly asserts auto_start remains. This corroborates prior public F6 rather than adding a new root cause. Coordinate the policy and migration if removal of session is intended.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12246#issuecomment-5835821818), checked at head `74f1d5b` ("Only remove the UEFI Limine unsigned-overwrite hook"). That commit changes only `migrations/1789639200.sh` and its test. It fixes two of the three parts of the hook-migration finding. The other earlier findings are in code this commit did not touch, and they still apply.

| Earlier finding | Status at `74f1d5b` |
|---|---|
| Hook migration deletes the BIOS deployment hook | **Resolved.** The hook is removed only when it contains `BOOTX64.EFI`. |
| Re-sign check runs as the invoking user | **Resolved** for the loader at `/boot/EFI/limine/limine_x64.efi`, now checked with `as_root test -f`. |
| Fresh ISO installs never run the migration | **Still present.** The omarchy-iso `quattro` branch (`86c0778`) still writes the UEFI hook, and new installs mark every migration as done. |
| Thunderbolt opt-out, Limine prune tool, ESP free-space check, SDDM keyring | **Still present.** The code is unchanged. |
| `/boot` permissions migration | **Still present.** The code is unchanged. In addition, when a single space follows `vfat`, the guard at `migrations/1789231611.sh:12` skips a `/boot` line that sets only one of `fmask` or `dmask`. The awk also skips any line that already has `fmask=`. In those cases the missing mask is never set. The earlier suggestion (handle each mask independently) covers this. |
| Optional test improvement for `update-disk-space-test.sh` | **Still present.** The test is unchanged. |

**Related open PR:** #13462 ("Preflight the ESP free space before an update") rewrites the same part of `bin/omarchy-update-requires-free-space`. It sizes the ESP check at twice the largest UKI and reads `ESP_PATH` differently, while this PR uses a fixed 300 MiB. It also extends `test/shell.d/update-disk-space-test.sh`. A three-way merge of the two heads conflicts in both files. Whichever lands second will need the ESP check and its fixtures reconciled.

**Verified:** the five PR tests pass at `74f1d5b` and on a merge into the current `quattro` tip (`3faafba`). The new BIOS-hook test fails against the previous migration. The hooks for the table below were generated by running omarchy-iso's own hook-writer functions in a sandbox. The migration then ran against each generated hook, with `sudo` and `sbctl` stubbed:

| ISO hook variant (same file name) | `Exec` copies `BOOTX64.EFI`? | Migration at `74f1d5b` |
|---|---|---|
| UEFI, ESP at `/boot` | yes | removed |
| UEFI, free-space install with ESP at `/efi` | yes | removed |
| UEFI removable path (`EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI`) | yes | removed |
| BIOS (`limine bios-install` + `limine-bios.sys`) | no | kept |

Once the hook is gone, limine-entry-tool's `limine-install` updates `<ESP>/EFI/limine/limine_x64.efi`, and its `90-limine-enroll-config` post hook signs it when sbctl has keys. This holds on each layout the ISO configurator produces (limine-entry-tool 1.40.0 source).

**Optional test improvement:** `limine-unsigned-hook-migration-test.sh` still passes when `as_root` is removed from the new `test -f "$efi"` check, which restores the root-only ESP bug. The fixture's `sudo` stub runs as the same user, and the EFI file is readable by that user. A case that makes the EFI file unreadable without the stub (or asserts that `sudo test -f <efi>` was called) would catch it.

### Re-sign step: `sbctl sign -s` adds the loader to sbctl's file list

This responds to the [comment on the re-sign step](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12246#issuecomment-5850271087). Checked against sbctl 0.18 and master, limine-entry-tool 1.40.0, and pacman 7.1.0 source:

- **Correct:** with sbctl 0.18, `sign -s` saves the file to sbctl's list only when it actually signs it. A file that is already signed returns early (`sbctl.go:129-178`). sbctl's pacman hook runs `sbctl sign-all`, which then signs whatever unsigned file stands at that path. The upstream commit `ae9c895` saves the file even when it is already signed, and it is not in any release yet.
- **Correct:** `90-limine-enroll-config` already signs the loader after every `limine-install` and kernel or initramfs run, with plain `sbctl sign` when sbctl has keys. Limine's `USAGE.md` confirms that a signed loader with no enrolled config checksum boots under Secure Boot without checking `limine.conf`.
- **Too broad:** "every … Limine upgrade" triggers `zz-sbctl.hook`. That is not true for a Limine-only transaction. The Arch `limine` package ships upper-case `BOOT*.EFI` files, pacman matches hook targets case-sensitively, and the hook's `*.efi*` target therefore does not match (the premise of #10945). Kernel, ucode and similar transactions do trigger it.
- **Too broad:** "after sbctl's next release every machine with sbctl would get the row." That applies only to machines that run this one-time migration after such a release, that have sbctl keys, and that keep the loader at `/boot`.

The change in this commit makes the line matter more. The old `[[ -f $efi ]]` was false on the ISO's root-only ESP, so `sbctl sign -s` rarely ran there. `as_root test -f` now makes it run. The loader is unsigned at migration time in exactly the case this migration targets: the ISO hook has just copied the raw binary over it. In that case the migration also signs a loader that is not sealed. With `ENABLE_ENROLL_LIMINE_CONFIG=yes` (opt-in, not an Omarchy default), the result boots under Secure Boot without checking `limine.conf`, where the firmware would otherwise refuse the unsigned file. The path is also fixed at `/boot`, so on a free-space install with the ESP at `/efi` the migration signs nothing. There the loader stays unsigned until the next Limine or kernel operation.

**Impact:** on Secure Boot installs where the hook had overwritten the loader, the migration adds a permanent entry to sbctl's list. Where config enrollment is enabled, it leaves a signed but unsealed loader.

**Suggested change:** replace the re-sign line with limine-entry-tool's own step, `as_root limine-enroll-config`, as the other comment proposes. It resolves `ESP_PATH` the same way `limine-install` does, seals when enrollment is enabled, and signs without `-s`. It exits non-zero when `ESP_PATH` is not a mounted vfat ESP, and in 1.40.0 also when enrollment or signing fails, and migrations run under `bash -euo pipefail`. So guard it (for example, run it only when the UEFI hook was removed) and keep `|| true`. At minimum, drop `-s`. That avoids the sbctl list entry but still signs an unsealed loader where enrollment is enabled. With `limine-enroll-config`, the test's `grep -Fq 'sbctl sign'` and its `-s` log assertions would change; dropping `-s` changes only the latter.

### A failed `sudo` now completes the migration and keeps the hook

`if [[ -e $hook ]] && as_root grep -Fq 'BOOTX64.EFI' "$hook"` treats a failed `sudo` (exit 1) the same as "no match" (grep exit 1). Inside the `if`, `set -e` does not stop the script:

```text
                       previous migration          74f1d5b
sudo fails (stubbed)   rm fails, exit 1            grep "no match", exit 0
UEFI hook              kept                        kept
omarchy-migrate        retries on next run         writes the marker, never retries
```

**Impact:** this affects a standalone `omarchy-migrate` run where sudo fails, for example after wrong passwords or with no TTY. `omarchy update` on the current `quattro` tip authorizes sudo before running migrations, so that path is not affected.

**Suggested change:** read the hook without `sudo` (the ISO writes it with default permissions), so a sudo failure still stops at `rm`. Alternatively, check `sudo` separately and exit non-zero when it fails.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `74f1d5b` on `quattro` `d201fb9`, also merged into the `quattro` tip `3faafba`. Source review of the new commit and of the dependencies it relies on: omarchy-iso `quattro` `86c0778`, limine-entry-tool 1.40.0, sbctl 0.18 and master, pacman 7.1.0, Limine 12.9.1 and omarchy-pkgs. The PR's tests, the migration probes (using hooks generated from the ISO's own code) and a test mutation ran in a sandbox. `sudo`, `sbctl` and the root-only ESP were stubbed or emulated. No real signing, config enrollment, pacman transaction or Secure Boot boot was performed. The findings in unchanged code were rechecked for changes, not re-tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
